📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The viral story of a grandmother who accidentally invited a stranger to Thanksgiving dinner is being turned into a Lifetime movie, nearly 10 years after their unlikely friendship began.

Wanda Dench and Jamal Hinton first made headlines in 2016 when a mistaken text message led to the pair celebrating Thanksgiving together. What started as an accidental invitation has since become an annual tradition, with the two continuing to reunite for the holiday.

Now, their friendship is heading to television after the pair signed a deal with Lifetime to bring their story to the screen, with a movie expected to arrive in November 2027.

Dench confirmed to The Arizona Republic on November 16 that she and Hinton recently signed over the rights to their story for a Lifetime movie at the moment titled ‘The Thanksgiving Grandma.’.

The film is expected to begin production in early 2027, with producer Jack Leslie targeting a November release that same year.

“They did tell us right up front that it’s based on our story,” Dench explained.

Hinton also revealed the news on Instagram, sharing a photo alongside Dench and celebrating their partnership with Lifetime.

“Very excited to officially be in business with Lifetime!” he wrote. “They believe in our story, and it truly feels like we’re in the best hands as we take this next step.”.

He also thanked Dench for being a constant source of support throughout their friendship, telling followers that their journey was only getting started.

In a recent development, the pair’s story began in November 2016 when Dench accidentally texted Hinton while attempting to invite her grandson to Thanksgiving dinner. Unbeknownst to her, her grandson had changed his phone number, and Hinton received the invitation instead.

After exchanging messages and photos, the two realized they were strangers. However, Hinton jokingly asked whether he could still attend dinner.

“Of course you can, that’s what grandmas do … feed everyone,” Dench responded.

Their exchange quickly went viral on Twitter, and Hinton ultimately joined Dench and her family for Thanksgiving at her home in Arizona.

The tradition has continued every year since, with the pair sharing updates about their friendship on social media.

The upcoming Lifetime movie has been in development in various forms for years. Leslie initially approached Dench about adapting the story in 2018 while working at Netflix, but the project was eventually abandoned following downsizing at the firm.

Screenwriter Glen Dolman is now working on the Lifetime adaptation and recently spent a weekend at Dench’s home to learn more about their relationship.

“It’s going to be more of how we’ve supported each other throughout the 10 years,” Dench explained.

AI data center power demand will double by 2030 thanks to $4 trillion in spending, adding an entire Great Britain to energy strain

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (590 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the AI data center build-out is pushing electricity grids across the globe, with many regions facing demand from projects that would exceed the current peak load that each system could support.
  • Sources indicate that this massive power consumption is one of the reasons for the opposition against their construction in communities, with residents blaming them for increased utility prices.
  • Industry observers note that emissions are another issue that the IEA has raised.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the AI data center build-out is pushing electricity grids across the globe, with many regions facing demand from projects that would exceed the current peak load that each system could support. According to the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) World Energy Outlook 2026 report, a total of 120GW of capacity is currently available across all types of data centers across the globe, with another 120GW expected to be completed by the end of the decade, 75% of which would be dedicated to artificial intelligence. Aside from that, it’s also tracking 93 large “AI factories” that are either under construction or being expanded via satellite imagery. It estimates that the capacity for these sites grew from under 2GW to 17GW in just two years, and that they’re expected to hit a total of 50GW upon completion, the equivalent of adding a second Great Britain to power demand.

Sources indicate that this massive power consumption is one of the reasons for the opposition against their construction in communities, with residents blaming them for increased utility prices. However, the IEA states that its analysis “does not yet show a clear relationship between growth in data center capacity and increases in electricity prices.” It noted that if a data center uses existing capacity and pays for its share of the cost, then it could potentially lead to lower utility bills for all customers. However, if the grid operator is required to upgrade its system to accommodate the large consumer, then it could also lead to increased monthly bills if the costs are spread across all people.

Industry observers note that emissions are another issue that the IEA has raised. Renewable energy dominates data centers’ power purchase agreements at nearly 50%, but actual power generation puts coal- and natural-gas power sources closer to 60%. This is likely due to the need for reliability, with the latter kicking in when the former cannot deliver the power that the data center needs. Aside from that, a few projects are deploying their own power, like Elon Musk’s Colossus 2 in Southaven, Mississippi, with about 180GW planned or under construction in the U.S. So, even though renewable energy is growing to accommodate demand, it’s also expected that coal- and natural-gas emissions from data centers will rise by 70% by 2030.

Sources indicate that investments in AI data centers are expected to hit $32 trillion by 2050, putting the infrastructure spending for the industry larger than railways, electrification, and the internet, combined. Despite that, the IEA states the grid remains a significant bottleneck — renewable power plants take between one and five years to complete, which is around the same time that some massive data center projects take if they do not face an extended moratorium, while transmission works can take three to five times longer. This is probably one of the reasons why some AI hyperscalers are choosing to put jet engines on their sites instead, although these are also facing shortages, especially in turbine blades.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin has sued sweepstakes casino operator VGW and prediction market Kalshi on the same day, alleging illegal gambling under state law.
  • Recent findings suggest that arkansas has opened a two-front legal fight against online gambling it says is unlicensed.
  • Both cases allege illegal gambling and violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin has sued sweepstakes casino operator VGW and prediction market Kalshi on the same day, alleging illegal gambling under state law. The VGW complaint puts a dollar figure on the state's sweepstakes market and adds Arkansas to a growing list of states challenging the dual-currency model.

Recent findings suggest that arkansas has opened a two-front legal fight against online gambling it says is unlicensed. One lawsuit targets VGW, the firm behind Chumba Casino, LuckyLand and Global Poker. The other targets KalshiEX LLC and Kalshi Inc., the companies that own the Kalshi prediction market.

Both cases allege illegal gambling and violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. Both also include an unjust enrichment claim. In each case the state seeks restitution, penalties, taxes and injunctive relief.

The VGW suit attacks the Gold Coin/Sweeps Coin model that almost every US sweepstakes casino relies on. It names ten affiliated VGW companies. The complaint claims VGW reported about $66 million in taxable Arkansas sales between July 2025 and June 2026 and paid about $6 million in sales and use tax over that period, Gaming.net reported.

Those figures show a tech giant declaring sales to the state and paying tax on them. Yet VGW holds no Arkansas casino license, the state alleges. The complaint also accuses VGW of letting 18-year-olds play, even though Arkansas casinos require players to be 21.

According to recent reports, the case lands less than two months after the Newly introduced York settlement. New York Attorney General Letitia James revealed that deal on September 9, 2026. It covered Chumba Casino, Global Poker and Luckyland Slots. VGW’s coin-based games were already off the table for New Yorkers by then, after her office sent the tech giant a cease-and-desist letter in June 2025.

Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman went to court a few months earlier, claiming VGW’s sweepstakes casinos break Kentucky gambling law. Florida has also moved against dual-currency sweepstakes since June 2026. Arkansas now joins Kentucky, Florida and Newly introduced York on that list. For operators using the same coin structure, the pattern points to rising legal exposure state by state.

In a recent development, the Kalshi complaint rests on a constitutional definition. The Arkansas Constitution’s definition of casino gaming expressly covers accepting wagers on sporting events. Kalshi has never held a casino-gaming license from the state commission, the state alleges. Nor has it held any other Arkansas authorization to take sports wagers.

It has been revealed that the complaint expressly limits itself to state-law claims and relief under Arkansas law. That choice means the state is relying on its own consumer-protection statute rather than waiting on the CFTC. Money lost, betting that gets out of hand, and depression or other damage to mental health are dangers Kalshi understands its customers face, Griffin’s office said.

Today I filed a lawsuit against VGW, an online gaming platform that features such games as @ChumbaCasino, LuckyLand Casino, @LuckyLandSlots, and @official_glp.

Arkansas’s gambling laws are clear. If you’re providing a means for Arkansans to gamble money within our state, you are… pic.twitter.com/qs2dhRMC8K.

— Attorney General Tim Griffin (@AGTimGriffin) November 4, 2026.

Filing both cases on the same day signals how Arkansas views the two products. The attorney general is treating sweepstakes casinos and sports event contracts as the same kind of unlicensed gambling. Other states may weigh whether to copy that approach.

The VGW case was filed in White County Circuit Court. The Kalshi case was filed in Independence County Circuit Court.

“Discord kitten” is internet slang tied to flirting and role-play on the chat platform. The nickname became a running joke across Reddit, Twitter, and TikTok, referring to a romantic partner whom someone interacts with primarily through Discord.

The interaction left viewers divided, with some calling an AI Discord kitten “dystopian” while others seem genuinely excited by the idea, and have asked for a release date.

#23981. Playing GTA 6 this weekend? Here's 16 spoiler-free tips for your first playthrough

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1792 w)

Playing GTA 6 this weekend? Here's 16 spoiler-free tips for your first playthrough

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's launch weekend for GTA 6 - in case you hadn't noticed - and since I've played the best part of a hundred hours of this thing, I thought it might be useful to share a few pieces of advice from my time with it.
  • Many of these are most applicable for the early game, but there are a few that'll be worth bearing in mind throughout.
  • The below list is spoiler-free, so you can relax if you're anxious about going through the story entirely fresh.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's launch weekend for GTA 6 - in case you hadn't noticed - and since I've played the best part of a hundred hours of this thing, I thought it might be useful to share a few pieces of advice from my time with it.

Many of these are most applicable for the early game, but there are a few that'll be worth bearing in mind throughout. After last night's driving around I would also maybe add in a quick bonus one, come to think of it: watch out for cyclists making last-minute left turns. Or don't, actually. Half of this lot deserve it….

The below list is spoiler-free, so you can relax if you're anxious about going through the story entirely fresh. Though naturally I do explain the way some parts of this game work, taking away some of the sense of discovery. You can take my word for it that there's plenty more to discover beyond this though, so worry not.

If you'd like even more help navigating Leonida, then check out our wonderful guide team's GTA 6 walkthrough.

Sources indicate that the number one thing I'd tell people to do in GTA 6 is to create lots of save files and, as you progress and start needing to overwrite them, to try to keep a roughly even spread of files through each chapter. There are various reasons for this - for one, while the game autosaves, it doesn't seem to do that successfully if you suddenly lose power to the console or witness a rare game crash, so it'll preserve your progress. More than that: GTA's story and missions are surprisingly, perhaps mysteriously reactive. Quite a lot can differ, and so being able to go back and make different choices, or play the game differently, will be something 'future you' likely appreciates.

In the very early game you won't have access to a bank account, but once you do: you should put every bit of cash you have in there as soon as you can. Cash is lost on death or arrest - which can happen quite often in GTA 6, funnily enough - and there's no real benefit to carrying it around. Just about everything, besides in-game strippers, can be paid for via your BuckMe account directly. And there's a relatively low $20,000 limit you really don't want to hit in the middle of raiding a gang hideout, either.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 has a luxurious range of customisation settings, from hiding notifications about your relationship to reinstating the old 'tap to sprint' control scheme. The accessibility settings - while crucially I'm not an expert - seem considerable. And there are somewhat disguised difficult settings here around enemy damage taken and encounters with the police.

Fairly early in the game you'll gain access to the Scooter Bros. App, which lets you repair or summon your owned vehicles at will. Crucially, there's also an option to pay a one-off fee to unlock three free uses of the app per day. At $12,000, in the early game this is a lot of dosh, but once you rack up that kind of money after advancing through the game a little, it's well worth the initial cost. The sooner you unlock it, the more value it provides over time on a cost-per-use basis. And trust me when I say: as the game's intensity ramps up, you will probably find yourself needing to repair and recover your vehicles quite often. (Also, in Chapter 1, before you get access to the app, you can access the same service by going to your phone's contacts and calling Joey - handy!).

Rockstar has somewhat disincentivised it by adding a cost and putting it in your phone's apps rather than the main map screen, but you can fast travel around Leonida if you ever want or need to. This is done via the RideMe Uber-like app. It's not cheap - you'll need to pay both the fee for the journey and an additional $100 to skip that journey and instantly arrive at your destination, but in certain scenarios it might prove useful. To skip the journey, hold L2/LT once in the cab, and then hold down Triangle/Y when the option is shown. However….

Sources indicate that while it's possible to journey-skip your way around this world, having tested that first hand I'd advise against it. It might be obvious, but GTA 6 is genuinely designed around you manually travelling around, typically in the car. If you skip all your commutes between missions or locations, you'll miss out on the game's dozens and dozens of emergent events, which lead to anything from one-off jokes to entire mission chains. The car is also, in a way, kind of the heart of the entire game. Relish the intentional slowness!

Industry observers note that again, avoiding spoilers here, but in the mid game the 'true' loop of GTA 6 gameplay will properly reveal itself, in all the many methods of earning money and the increased emphasis on doing so. You can of course play the game however you like, but having reached the end and looked back from that point, I found that if there was a particular moment to set aside as the time for aimlessly exploring the world, it was from around Chapter 3 onwards. You'll have enough tools to be able to see it at more or less its fullest then, but also won't have missed anything essential by waiting until that point to take your foot off the pedal either.

A handy early-game tip here that even I missed when I was playing, but have since discovered: two islands in the small cluster of them to the south-west of Jason's early game home each house a really useful weapon, in a silenced pistol and a handy shotgun. You'll own these permanently once found, and so they can be incredibly helpful for navigating missions with maximum or minimal violence. Look for shipwrecks on those islands to find them. The pistol is hidden under a little hatch on the deck of a shipwreck on the southernmost point of the south-easternmost island. The shotgun is next to a small wooden wrecked boat around the middle of the northernmost island.

Recent findings suggest that A mechanic I slightly underused at first was the ability to 'save' a given outfit to your car. You can do this either from your car's trunk or from the wardrobe, and it's hugely useful as you start to get into more elaborate scrapes with the police (and also if you just like to role-play a bit and don the right outfit for the right occasion).

There are lots of reasons for this, from the moments of intimacy it affords you with your partner, to the extra buffs you can get from resting. Sleep at home, for instance, and you can then immediately pet your snake (ahem), down a coffee or drink from the fridge, grab an apple and take a shower for a range of buffs across health, stamina, and focus. Each of these will last quite some time, so it's worth the few minutes of time to do them. Eating and drinking regularly also helps you maximise gains in the gym.

It has been revealed that rockstar seems to enjoy the concept of a game within a game, and that's exemplified well by the in-game phone. You can find missions via scrolling Snapmatic, it's in-game social media, or from texting various contacts you pick up as the game progresses. It's worth checking it every now and then just to see if anything interesting - or just funny or absurd - might pop up.

It has been revealed that car trunks, both those belonging to the public and the police, are often well worth a look. Even if you're quickly nabbing a car for a short-term dash, take a moment to check the boot for anything worthwhile. We've found everything from sellable narcotics to very useful weapons in there. In cop cars, that goes up several notches, too.

A small thing, but in-mission checkpoints are relatively generous in GTA 6. If you really wanted to complete a mission a certain way - undetected or non-violent, say - then don't be afraid to quickly re-load rather than feeling you need to manually load up an earlier save, or give up on your goal entirely. It's also helped me out with a few minor progress-jamming bugs along the way too.

This might seem obvious, but it's worth emphasising for early-game players: it's very, very rare that you actually need to kill anybody in GTA 6. Enemies are fully incapacitated when you see a yellow hit marker over your crosshairs, even if that just comes from blasting away at their toes. If you make a habit of navigating combat this way then that also makes it much easier to recover your 'Professional' criminal status if you ever do decide to go full rampage. Though you can, of course, ultimately play this game however you like. Just be aware there may be consequences, known and unknown, as you go. Also: don't forget to click the right analog stick to aim down sights - it's an easy thing to forget when playing a third-person shooter like this, and not always the best way to operate, but incredibly helpful in select circumstances.

Throughout the game you'll have a 'family savings' goal to hit. As you progress you'll find more ways to earn money much faster, and so it's easy to make up for lost time here if, later on, you decide that actually you do want to think about the future after all. But that grind will be a fair bit less painful if you chip away at the target as you go. As long as you save yourself some fun money - a few hundred in the early game, few thousand in the mid game, and a few tens of thousands late on - then you'll have enough to do key things like buying latest garages to register vehicles, or paying to register them themselves.

Recent findings suggest that throughout your time with GTA 6 you'll encounter moments when you need to make a choice. Interestingly, I noticed at least a few occasions where a scenario changed when I just waited, doing nothing at all. Sometimes that might mean a choice is made for you - so waiting is a risk - but on other occasions newly introduced options become available. Sometimes they might mean a genuinely different consequence, others they might just lead to characters reacting in a certain kind of way. But it's worth experimenting - your first options aren't always your only ones.

Tech Report: New Windows 11 lock screen zero-day unlocks BitLocker-protected PCs with just a few keystrokes

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, considering the current status of the cybersecurity landscape, some may well say that "0-day" has lost its meaning, The latest high-stakes vulnerability pertains to a bug in Windows 11 (and possibly 10), wherein an attacker can partially bypass the lock screen and run software as the logged-in user, and seemingly access their data.
  • In a recent development, unsurprisingly, the bug was discovered by Abdelhamid Naceri, the prolific Windows hacker known to the world as Nightmare Eclipse, and is responsible for about a dozen zero-day findings in Microsoft's operating system.
  • Sources indicate that to trigger the vulnerability, all you need is a keyboard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, considering the current status of the cybersecurity landscape, some may well say that "0-day" has lost its meaning, The latest high-stakes vulnerability pertains to a bug in Windows 11 (and possibly 10), wherein an attacker can partially bypass the lock screen and run software as the logged-in user, and seemingly access their data. If true, the vulnerability means even BitLocker won't help keep users' files protected.

In a recent development, unsurprisingly, the bug was discovered by Abdelhamid Naceri, the prolific Windows hacker known to the world as Nightmare Eclipse, and is responsible for about a dozen zero-day findings in Microsoft's operating system. The exploit requires physical access to the machine, but that's precisely the scenario that lock screens and/or BitLocker are supposed to protect against.

Sources indicate that to trigger the vulnerability, all you need is a keyboard. In the Windows 11 lock screen, click "Forgot my PIN," then hit Win+U to bring up the voice narrator. The window will be hidden behind the lock screen, which, for practical purposes, is just a veneer, but you can interact with it using the keyboard if you hold down the Caps Lock key and use the arrows and Enter.

After some brief navigation through Narrator, you'll actually be in Settings, and then have multiple avenues for further shenanigans. One obvious one is going into Bluetooth and Devices and setting Autoplay to show a USB stick's files and folders, then plugging in your own with your software of choice to run. Additionally, on a personal machine, the user is bound to have administrator permissions, so you can just create your own account.

According to recent reports, this bug is quite fresh, so there isn't widespread reporting or testing. The author claims "the vulnerability seems to be extremely consistent in every machine I tested it in." We did encounter a sysadmin on Reddit, danrhodes1987, who claims they've tested it on machines they manage, and sure enough, it works, though only on their InTune-enrolled devices. He states that "you can launch anything you want in the context of the user logged onto the device.".

Additionally, they found it possible to invisibly navigate whichever programs the user had open before they locked their screen, which all but guarantees that the victim's entire data and programs will be fully accessible. As a Windows sysadmin friend of mine remarked, Windows' lock screen implementation always felt like a kludge, and he posits this won't be the last hack found for it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that fanDuel's US adjusted EBITDA nearly disappeared in the third quarter of 2026, even as US revenue rose 6%. Flutter blamed spending on FanDuel Predicts and its Alberta launch, while FanDuel Casino's revenue growth slowed to 8%.

According to recent reports, fanDuel’s US business barely turned a profit in the third quarter of 2026. US adjusted EBITDA came in at just $3 million, against $51 million a year earlier. Revenue moved the other way, climbing 6% to $1.455 billion. Flutter blamed spending on FanDuel Predicts and its launch in Alberta.

For the regulated US market, the result shows how much prediction-market spending is costing one of its online leaders. The parent company also lowered its full-year outlook for 2026. Buybacks are on hold for the foreseeable future so Flutter can focus on organic investment and paying down debt. Leverage stood at 4.6x at the end of the quarter, up from 3.7x in December 2025.

In a recent development, the group’s net loss widened to $1.148 billion from $789 million a year earlier. That figure includes impairments tied to Brazil, where Flutter stopped operating on Sept. 26, 2026.

FanDuel Casino is adding players much faster than it is adding revenue. Flutter pointed to competition and to slower growth as US iGaming states mature. The contrast with late 2025 is sharp. In the fourth quarter of 2025, FanDuel Casino grew revenue 33% and held 28% of US iGaming gross gaming revenue.

Flutter put that share at 27% for the three months to Sept. 30, the same level it reported for the second quarter. An outside estimate is lower. FanDuel’s iGaming share was 25.1%, down from 26.6% a year earlier, according to Citizens figures published by NEXT.io. The same figures revealed US iGaming growth slowing to 12% year over year in the third quarter, the lowest on record.

It has been revealed that sportsbook revenue grew 4%. FanDuel’s share of US sportsbook gross gaming revenue slipped to 36%, from 39% in the second quarter. Its share of handle was 33%.

According to recent reports, the product drawing the investment is gaining consumers. Trading volume on FanDuel Predicts rose 102% from the prior quarter to $119 million. CEO Dan Taylor said the app had 140,000 active users in October.

Flutter reiterates $50m prediction market revenue target for 2026:.

Flutter's FanDuel Predicts reached 140,000 active users in October as its parent maintained its $40m adjusted EBITDA forecast for market-making.

Full Story ➡️ https://t.co/B7KSlEgH0a pic.twitter.com/zKXX8fV2fG.

— NEXTpredict (@nextpredictio) November 4, 2026.

Alberta is the other latest cost. FanDuel reached more than 20% of the gaming market there in its first quarter. Management noted that was well ahead of its pace after launching in Ontario.

Together, the figures are consistent with a firm trading near-term US profit for growth in newer markets and products. Taylor took over as CEO from Peter Jackson on Oct. 1, 2026. Buybacks will stay paused until leverage falls to a range of 2 to 2.5 times, a target he set for a period of about 24 months.

#23977. I completed GTA 6's indie game darling pastiche, Tenebrae Lux, and all I got was this lousy sense of accomplishment

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1288 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

I completed GTA 6's indie game darling pastiche, Tenebrae Lux, and all I got was this lousy sense of accomplishment

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1288 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that "We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance.
  • Developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal.
  • The first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that "We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance. Voyaging uncharted waters may appear foolish to some, yet folly and heroism can often appear the same to the undiscerning eye," so says the voice of Johannes Zuch - creator, writer, director, composer, and 'perceptual architect' behind Leonida's latest favourite indie darling art game, Tenebrae Lux. It's pretentious, it's deeply up its own arse, and it's awkward and off-putting to play. A must-review for Eurogamer.

Developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal. Jason is quick to dismiss Tenebrae Lux in firm, but once Cal slinks off home - hungover and dreary - I slide the disc back into my JoyStation console and sink my teeth back into it. Jason loves this stuff, really. He only keeps Time Jackers: Rewind installed so his mates don't judge him.

The first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name. It's Latin for 'darkness and light', or something similar. Is this riffing on Clair Obscur, which is French for 'light dark'? No, it's too cerebral for that - too plodding and navel-gazey. Sandfall Interactive wouldn't be this pretentious. Maybe it's a pastiche of Dear Esther, then, drawing on the tenets and schema of the 'walking simulator' genre and using that washed-out film noir aesthetic. But then, it's too wordy for that, with too many interactive and puzzle-adjacent elements. Ah, it must be mocking The Witness, instead - there's the telltale lighthouse, the 'I'm definitely not telling you where to go and what to do' internal narration, and of course the fingerprints of Johannes Zuch are all over it. Johannes Zuch, Jonathan Blow - see how they braided them together? (Sorry).

Sources indicate that whilst this has been created by Rockstar as a pastiche - as much loving send-up as it is withering take down - and designed to make a quick joke in the early 'Feng Shui' mission, the game is playable from start to finish if you so desire. You boot it up by inserting a physical disc, too, which is funny given the context. And it's good! Well, not good good, but it's a proper brainteaser, and ribs 2016's The Witness with such knowledge and (I think?) respect that it's hard not to be charmed by Rockstar's game-within-a-game. There are collectibles to be found that riff on Mark Z. Danielewski's House of Leaves, too, a knowing nod to the most try-hard of all try-hard literature.

Within seconds of the title screen, too, you're presented with a game-within-a-game-within-a-game. You must clear four boards filled with puzzle pieces as the protagonist mutters something mysterious and weird in his posh voice. Do so, and you unlock the door to the next location. Head up to a bunker, and you'll see a room filled with various clues - maybe it's a flashing lamp flickering in morse code, maybe it's a malfunctioning clock presenting a maths puzzle, maybe it's a pricetag on a record that changes on every visit, maybe it's a photograph with anomalous elements, maybe it's a "Developed Using Zuchworks Engine" easter egg hidden in the environment. You need to keep your wits about you, because one of these clues changes every time you enter - and the clue corresponds to a date that changes on a calendar on the wall.

In a recent development, you can look up a guide if you need to, or you can spend far too long figuring out how all this relates to the telephone you can find in the room on your own, like muggins here, before opening up the path to the next puzzle. Look at the image below to see the level of record-keeping and brainteasing this bizarre little game prompted from me. I will say, the sense of achievement you get from playing around with this stuff is pretty remarkable, given - let's not forget I'm actually playing Grand Theft Auto 6 whilst I'm wandering around in the black and white murk trying to complete a puzzle game for no actual reward.

The bunker room is, by far, the hardest part of Tenebrae Lux. From here, things ease up: you need to figure out the right sequence of glyphs on a bridge, and then put some distance between yourself and a curious and rather creepy suited man that's seemingly figuring things out ahead of you in a location inspired by, I think, The Backrooms (or Portal, or Superliminal, or maybe something else entirely. Who knows what Zuch was thinking?).

"With the last enigma finally mastered," the narrator drones in his bumbling monotone, "I step forward into the void, the shadows swallow, consuming all, and then finally the sweet embrace of darkness of which there is no end." 'You have just experienced a Johannes Zuch experience', Tenebrae Lux tells me, before cutting to the best joke of the whole thing: the credits roll much akin to something Hideo Kojima would produce.

It has been revealed that so, what do you get out of all of this? Well - just like real puzzle games in the real world - nothing, really. If you've not completed one of the other three fully playable games in GTA 6, you will get a trophy/achievement. But given the main game is all about Jason and Lucia's desperate scramble to escape the poverty trap, to try and break free of the cycle of debt, violence, and consequence that keeps them clinging to Leonida's seedy underbelly, there's no monetary reward. There's no 'progress' in the sense of the protagonist's shared story.

Even in terms of your own cold, hard, mathematical 'completion' you only need to boot each of the four games up once in order to work towards GTA 6's 100% completion. So what's the point of all this? Why did I spend the better part of 90 minutes trying to figure out how to find a sliver of light in the dark in Tenebrae Lux? The game is a wonderful pastiche in that, essentially, it's not really saying anything. You can probably project some vague meaning onto it if you wish - I'm pretty certain the protagonist literally 'finds himself' at the end - but glib little readings like that are ten-a-penny in this genre.

I think the most impressive thing about Tenebrae Lux is that it exists. You're teased with it in an early mission - Rockstar may as well say 'look, we put a game in a game, lol' - but it's more than that. This is what happens when Rockstar's 4700-plus developers are given the room to… develop. Tenebrae Lux could very easily have been a non-interactive experience, a quick, cheap joke shown over-the-shoulder taking a drive-by pop shot at Johnathan Blow, Hideo Kojima, Dan Pinchbeck, or any and all of the above. Or maybe it could be a 'vertical slice', an incomplete demo, a teaser. But it's not, because nothing about GTA 6 is quick or cheap.

Industry observers note that GTA 6, in every single conceivable way, is a premium experience - part-sandbox, part-simulation, part-otherworld. To create not just one, but four fully playable and completable games within that framework is showboating, sure, but to make that game actually good and - perhaps controversially - even better than some of the games it's pastiching… Well, it's just rubbing salt in the wound, really.

A code for the game was provided by Cal Hampton.

Jimmy John’s is celebrating the holiday season with a limited-time meal inspired by National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation, featuring newly introduced menu items and exclusive collectibles based on the classic comedy.

Industry observers note that the sandwich chain has partnered with Warner Bros. to launch the Christmas Vacation Feast, bringing several references from the 1989 holiday film to its restaurants nationwide.

Beginning November 23, customers can order the themed meal at participating Jimmy John’s locations, with the promotion also extending beyond the menu through exclusive merchandise and a holiday-themed restaurant makeover in Chicago.

The Christmas Vacation Feast features three holiday-inspired menu items, custom packaging based on the movie, and a collectible turtleneck dickie inspired by Cousin Eddie.

A post shared by Markie_devo (@markie_devo).

Those interested in collecting all four Cousin Eddie-inspired dickies will be able to purchase them individually without ordering the complete meal.

“When it comes to the holidays, Clark Griswold set the bar impossibly high,” noted Suzanne DeRouchie, Vice President of Integrated Marketing Communications at Jimmy John’s.

“We wanted to capture that same over-the-top energy in a way only Jimmy John’s could. From festive latest menu items to the Cousin Eddie-inspired dickie, the Christmas Vacation Feast gives fans a delicious excuse to lean into a little holiday chaos.”.

Jimmy John’s is also transforming its restaurant at 501 N. LaSalle Drive in Chicago with 25,000 holiday lights, recreating one of the film’s most recognizable scenes.

The decorated restaurant will be on display from November 21 through December 26, paying tribute to the movie’s Chicago-area setting and the sandwich chain’s origins.

Burger King unveils Snoopy meals for adults and kids with exclusive Peanuts collectibles.

Jimmy John’s is giving away free Picklewiches to customers who dress as pickles.

McDonald’s reveals Home Alone Meal with pizza-flavored fries and collectible socks.

Additionally, a limited-edition merchandise collection will launch November 23 through the Jimmy Store, featuring a squirrel plushie, a Clark Griswold-inspired hockey jersey, and a Cousin Eddie-inspired trapper hat.

Jimmy John’s is the latest fast food chain to embrace holiday nostalgia, following McDonald’s Home Alone Meal, which features pizza-flavored fries and collectible socks, and Burger King’s Peanuts collaboration, which includes Snoopy-themed meals for adults and kids alongside exclusive holiday collectibles.

It took me less than an hour to find my first incredibly minor Rockstar easter egg in GTA 6 - but it has some major implications for Leonida

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (883 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Are you wondering how connected the worlds of GTA 5 and GTA 6 are?
  • It has been revealed that right, if you're reading from this point onwards, you're clearly here for the tea.
  • In a recent development, called 'Body Copy' - a joke I appreciate as a former magazine editor, naturally - this publication features a few different articles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Are you wondering how connected the worlds of GTA 5 and GTA 6 are? Well, I've got some news for you. Keep on reading below if you'd like some very minor spoilers for the early game of GTA 6, spoilers for GTA 5, as well as some information about how the upcoming game links to GTA 5 and other Rockstar games.

It has been revealed that right, if you're reading from this point onwards, you're clearly here for the tea. In the first hour or so of GTA 6, when you finally get control of Jason and head to your first property (the green stilted house) in the Leonida Keys, you will be able to explore a little. On my way to do a workout - you need to keep Jason a peak physical instrument for his work's sake, right? Right? - I happened upon a fitness magazine resting on a table on the decking out front.

In a recent development, called 'Body Copy' - a joke I appreciate as a former magazine editor, naturally - this publication features a few different articles. There's Morning Glory, where Nolan Crockett jacks you with his early workout; Skindecent Exposure, a photo spread about why beaches are 'crazy' places to work out; Shrediquette, a piece dedicated to proper in-gym decorum; and Twilight Tantra, an interview feature and yoga masterclass with 'gerontophile' Fabien LaRouche.

Industry observers note that hang on, Fabien LaRouche… isn't that the French wellness guru and shyster that was a "close friend" to Amanda De Santa in Grand Theft Auto 5? Yes, yes it is. In fact, Fabien played quite a large role in that game, acting as the antagonistic force that eventually fractured Michael and Amanda's relationship. After conducting an affair under the guise of 'yoga lessons', Amanda left our protagonist, and moved in with Fabien, taking Michael's kids - Jimmy and Tracy - with her. In a totally healthy and normal way, you could follow their new life via updates posted to GTA's Facebook surrogate, LifeInvader. It's clear the kids never liked the pretentious, annoying man - but for Amanda, the penny is a little slower to drop. Eventually, Amanda and Michael reconcile their differences - with the latter whalloping Fabien in the process. The married couple pledge to resolve their differences, and Fabien is never seen again.

According to recent reports, until GTA 6, at least. Here, in what we assume is supposed to be 2025 or 2026, it's been about 13 years since we last saw the character (it is widely agreed that GTA 5 is set in 2013 - the game's original launch year). And it seems that the events surrounding Michael and his family really did a number on Fabien. Which - of course - he blamed on the universe, rather than taking any personal responsibility. Naturally.

Sources indicate that "Ever since the karmic decay of Los Santos was made perfectly clear to him in the early 2010s, yoga instructor Fabien LaRouche has been on an epic pilgrimage of enlightenment through the remotest ashrams and finest 5-star resorts and plastic surgery retreats of The East," reads the Body Copy article. "Having completed his chakric education and returned to the United States, we meet with him on the final week of his six-month residency at Dwindle Wood Retirement Community.".

According to recent reports, here, the article goes on to explore Fabien's penchant for older women - he seems to like their nature, their desire to learn about self-improvement and wellness, and (perhaps most importantly) their bank accounts. "Being over the hill doesn't necessarily mean you have nothing left to live for," he opines in the article. Thanks for that, Fabien.

Recent findings suggest that it's interesting to see - very early in the game and quite plainly telegraphed - that Rockstar is willing to reintroduce us to people from previous games. This isn't a megaton addition by any means - Fabien was never a 'main character' - but I love that a nod to him, in a feature tucked away at the back of a magazine, sets the scene for more cameos, perhaps, later in the game. It shows us, nice and early, that GTA 5 and GTA 6 are indeed connected. By inference, then, we know that GTA 4 is included in that same picture; there were recurring characters in GTA 5 that appeared in GTA 4, after all - Patrick McReary, Johnny Klebitz, Rocco Pelosi and more come to mind.

Recent findings suggest that it may seem like a small thing, but it's just another example of Rockstar using its expansive toolset, ridiculous budget, and well-established legacy to inject a sense of scale into the world of Grand Theft Auto 6. There are other nods to the universe out there, too. I won't spoil them here, but I've been a little bit dewy-eyed to hear rumours of some of the other nods to Rockstar titles hidden in the world of Leonida: it makes all the experiences I've had in past games, the emotional response I've had to previous Rockstar worlds, feel in some way valid and meaningful here, too. I'm looking forward to seeing what other little secrets await me across the keys and into the glowing neon promise of Vice City proper.

  • This pattern places PENN within the slowing-iGaming-growth story running through this week’s US operator reports.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that PENN Entertainment's online segment grew revenue in the third quarter, but the gain came from passed-through partner gaming taxes, not from players. The segment now needs a positive fourth quarter to reach a full-year target that has already been lowered.

In a recent development, other revenues carried the whole of the Interactive segment’s third-quarter gain at PENN Entertainment. Segment revenue rose to $348.4 million from $297.7 million, while the third-party partner gaming-tax amounts booked there climbed to $191.4 million from $139.5 million a year earlier. Online gaming revenue itself fell 2.1% to $126.6 million from $129.3 million, as iCasino growth was offset by lower sports betting handle.

This pattern places PENN within the slowing-iGaming-growth story running through this week’s US operator reports.

The nine-month figures show the same reliance on the gross-up. Interactive revenue reached $1,056.0 million, up from $903.9 million. The tax gross-up within it rose to $562.7 million from $405.6 million.

Recent findings suggest that the group as a whole had a stronger quarter. Total revenue was $1,840.0 million. Net income came in at $32.6 million, against a $865.1 million net loss a year earlier. PENN also raised its full-year retail guidance to $5.89 billion in revenue and $1.973 billion in adjusted EBITDAR, increases of $16 million and $10 million.

Profitability is improving faster than revenue. The Interactive adjusted EBITDA loss for the first nine months shrank to $38.7 million from $227.6 million. PENN attributes that mainly to lower marketing, general and administrative, and labor costs.

Industry observers note that expansion has weighed on the quarter. PENN released theScore Bet, theScore Casino and standalone Hollywood iCasino apps in Alberta on July 13, 2026. Excluding that third-quarter launch investment, Interactive adjusted EBITDA improved quarter over quarter throughout 2026, management remarked on the earnings call.

Recent findings suggest that the standalone Hollywood iCasino brand is central to the plan. It posted record quarterly revenue in the second quarter. PENN is now leaning on its US growth, and on steady trends through October, to support the full-year Interactive target. That makes the brand a test for whether a mid-tier US online casino can turn profitable.

Industry observers note that the target itself has moved. In February, PENN guided the segment to breakeven adjusted EBITDA for 2026, which it described as a $268 million improvement from 2025. The cost of the Alberta launch is now built into a weaker outlook.

PENN Entertainment CEO Jay Snowden discussed the potential of more Canadian provinces launching iGaming on an earnings call today.

In the last month, Quebec, Upcoming Brunswick, and Nova Scotia have all shown interest in exploring commercial online gambling.https://t.co/8WqAPfw9LY.

— Tom Nightingale (@TNightingaming) November 5, 2026.

Sources indicate that land-based trends offer some support. CEO Jay Snowden mentioned PENN’s own Pennsylvania gaming revenue in October posted stronger year-over-year growth than in any other month of 2026. Most of that growth came in the second half of the month, after skill games were shut down. In his view, the midterm results could help PENN further by weakening support for skill-game machines.

The online segment still has to deliver. Reaching the revised target depends on Interactive turning its third-quarter loss into positive adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter.

The energy strategy most companies don’t have

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1415 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for trucking fleets, manufacturers, and other energy-intensive businesses, energy has been little more than a line item for the past two decades.
  • Industry observers note that for trucking fleets, manufacturers, and other energy-intensive businesses, energy has been little more than a line item for the past two decades.
  • Global energy use keeps growing and electricity demand is rising more than twice as fast as energy use overall, according to the International Energy Agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for trucking fleets, manufacturers, and other energy-intensive businesses, energy has been little more than a line item for the past two decades. Today it’s a competitive variable. Whether a business can secure the energy it needs—and afford it—increasingly determines whether it can grow. Global energy use keeps growing and electricity demand is rising more than twice as fast as energy use overall, according to the International Energy Agency. The problem is that war and geopolitical conflict, along with tariffs reshaping the cost of equipment, are affecting supply and cost. Policies are also shifting with election cycles. This year alone, oil swung from $118 a barrel to under $72 and back above $100, while Washington rewrote the nation’s fuel-economy rules. No single shock is decisive—the shocks compound. As a result, nearly every fleet and fuel-retail operator I speak with is wrestling with whether to use electric, diesel, or natural gas. However, energy markets are moving too fast and too unevenly for anyone to call it with confidence. The operators pulling ahead have stopped trying to choose one. Instead, they’re building the capability of running on more than one energy source—and deciding in real time which to use, where, and when. FedEx is a case in point. It now runs nearly 9,500 electric vehicles while testing renewable diesel for the long-haul trucks where, as the company puts it, “full electrification is not yet feasible at scale.” And it isn’t alone: Roughly 19% of North American fleets now operate EVs, and 30% run hybrid or alternative-fuel vehicles. PAY FOR FLEXIBILITY WHERE IT COUNTS Optionality isn’t free. A second energy source means added infrastructure, more complex procurement and, often, some loss of efficiency. No business can hedge everything. The discipline is deciding where flexibility is worth paying for. The most resilient operators I see ask two questions about every site, route, and asset: If this energy source were disrupted tomorrow, how much revenue would stop? And how exposed is it to a single fuel, supplier, or grid connection? Where both answers are high, redundancy is insurance worth buying now. A delivery depot that charges its entire fleet from one utility feed can’t run routes when that feed goes down. Where impact is high but exposure is modest, flexible supply contracts, rather than long-term agreements locking in a single source, may be enough. Where the impact is low, optimize for cost and move on. THE EASY PART IS THE HARDWARE Adding EV chargers to a forecourt or alternative-fuel trucks to a fleet is now easy. Running them together is not. A mixed-energy operation creates decisions a single-fuel business never faced. Which vehicle takes which route, given its charge level and the day’s energy prices? When should a depot charge its equipment to avoid peak demand costs? How do you compare cost per mile across diesel, natural gas, and electric when the data lives in separate systems? The advantage goes to businesses that can see their entire energy picture in one place and act on it. In a volatile market, the ability to switch is only as valuable as the ability to know when to switch. 3 MOVES WORTH MAKING NOW For leaders of fleet, fuel-retail, and other energy-intensive businesses, building a multi-energy operation starts with understanding where you’re vulnerable and what flexibility is worth. These three moves lay that groundwork. 1. Map your 24-hour exposure. Identify the sites, routes, and assets that would stop generating revenue within a day of losing their primary energy source. 2. Put a price on flexibility. Capital cases that compare only cost per gallon or per kilowatt-hour miss the value of being able to switch. Make the cost of downtime an explicit line in every energy investment. 3. Instrument before you diversify. You can’t coordinate what you can’t see. Bring fuel, charging, payments, and fleet data into a single view before adding the next energy source. Energy isn’t going to get more predictable. Leaders who build for adaptability will succeed whichever way it goes. As an executive, ask yourself: If your primary energy source were disrupted tomorrow, how promptly could your business respond? Mark Morelli is president and CEO of Vontier.

The problem is that war and geopolitical conflict, along with tariffs reshaping the cost of equipment, are affecting supply and cost. Policies are also shifting with election cycles. This year alone, oil swung from $118 a barrel to under $72 and back above $100, while Washington rewrote the nation’s fuel-economy rules. No single shock is decisive—the shocks compound.

Sources indicate that as a result, nearly every fleet and fuel-retail operator I speak with is wrestling with whether to use electric, diesel, or natural gas. However, energy markets are moving too fast and too unevenly for anyone to call it with confidence. The operators pulling ahead have stopped trying to choose one. Instead, they’re building the capability of running on more than one energy source—and deciding in real time which to use, where, and when.

Industry observers note that fedEx is a case in point. It now runs nearly 9,500 electric vehicles while testing renewable diesel for the long-haul trucks where, as the firm puts it, “full electrification is not yet feasible at scale.” And it isn’t alone: Roughly 19% of North American fleets now operate EVs, and 30% run hybrid or alternative-fuel vehicles.

Optionality isn’t free. A second energy source means added infrastructure, more complex procurement and, often, some loss of efficiency. No business can hedge everything. The discipline is deciding where flexibility is worth paying for.

It has been revealed that the most resilient operators I see ask two questions about every site, route, and asset: If this energy source were disrupted tomorrow, how much revenue would stop? And how exposed is it to a single fuel, supplier, or grid connection?

Sources indicate that where both answers are high, redundancy is insurance worth buying now. A delivery depot that charges its entire fleet from one utility feed can’t run routes when that feed goes down. Where impact is high but exposure is modest, flexible supply contracts, rather than long-term agreements locking in a single source, may be enough. Where the impact is low, optimize for cost and move on.

Adding EV chargers to a forecourt or alternative-fuel trucks to a fleet is now easy. Running them together is not.

A mixed-energy operation creates decisions a single-fuel business never faced. Which vehicle takes which route, given its charge level and the day’s energy prices? When should a depot charge its equipment to avoid peak demand costs? How do you compare cost per mile across diesel, natural gas, and electric when the data lives in separate systems?

According to recent reports, the advantage goes to businesses that can see their entire energy picture in one place and act on it. In a volatile market, the ability to switch is only as valuable as the ability to know when to switch.

For leaders of fleet, fuel-retail, and other energy-intensive businesses, building a multi-energy operation starts with understanding where you’re vulnerable and what flexibility is worth. These three moves lay that groundwork.

It has been revealed that 1. Map your 24-hour exposure. Identify the sites, routes, and assets that would stop generating revenue within a day of losing their primary energy source.

Industry observers note that 2. Put a price on flexibility. Capital cases that compare only cost per gallon or per kilowatt-hour miss the value of being able to switch. Make the cost of downtime an explicit line in every energy investment.

It has been revealed that 3. Instrument before you diversify. You can’t coordinate what you can’t see. Bring fuel, charging, payments, and fleet data into a single view before adding the next energy source.

According to recent reports, energy isn’t going to get more predictable. Leaders who build for adaptability will succeed whichever way it goes. As an executive, ask yourself: If your primary energy source were disrupted tomorrow, how rapidly could your business respond?

Mark Morelli is president and CEO of Vontier.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rep. Charlie Geren filed a constitutional amendment on the first filing day of Texas's 2027 session that would let voters decide on casinos and sports betting. A Democratic House and a supportive lieutenant governor-elect improve its odds, but a two-thirds Senate vote and a fight over the Senate's leadership stand in the way.

Texas lawmakers have their first gambling-expansion measures of the 2027 session. Rep. Charlie Geren, a Fort Worth Republican, filed House Joint Resolution 52 on November 9, the first day of bill filing, and Democratic Sen. Carol Alvarado filed a Senate resolution on casinos and sports betting, SJR 11, the same day. Voters would get the final say on a constitutional change giving lawmakers the power to permit and oversee casinos and sports betting.

The resolution would require lawmakers to limit casinos to a capped number of facilities statewide. Initial license terms would run at least 40 years. The Legislature would decide where sports betting could take place. The ballot wording would describe licensing, application fees and a tax on casino and sports wagering revenue at a limited number of locations.

In a recent development, geren framed a statewide vote as the end of the debate either way. A rejection at the ballot box would close the question permanently, he remarked.

It has been revealed that the political ground has moved since Geren’s last attempt. Democrats won control of the Texas House in the November 3 election. Republicans held on to the Senate. As a state representative, Goodwin backed the 2023 gambling measure. The office she won was held by Dan Patrick, who blocked gambling expansion for years.

The constitutional route keeps the bar high. An amendment needs two-thirds of both chambers, then a majority of voters. Approved amendments go on the November ballot after the session ends. In 2023, online sports betting passed the House with 101 votes. Geren’s casino resolution reached only 92. The casino measure fell short of the threshold that the betting measure cleared.

The Senate is the harder test. Republicans control the chamber, and any amendment needs two-thirds support there. On November 9, Patrick urged Republican senators on conservative radio to strip Goodwin of her powers as Senate president before she takes office. Her influence over the chamber, including any gambling bill, now hangs on that fight.

According to recent reports, goodwin has signaled a conciliatory approach. Her transition team said she wants to work with Republican senators and believes Texas is “best served by a deliberative, collaborative body.”.

Recent findings suggest that texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, arguably the casino and sports betting industry's biggest boogeyman in the Lone Star State, will leave office next year. What comes next in a crucial 2027 for the largest remaining state without major casino gaminghttps://t.co/u6WLlaAj3S.

— Ryan Butler (@butlerbetstrade) November 4, 2026.

Industry money has struggled to change the Republican map. In the March primaries, anti-gambling incumbents beat challengers backed by the Las Vegas Sands-funded Texas Sands PAC and Texas Defense PAC, to which Miriam Adelson had given $9 million. Even so, Texas Sands PAC has pledged to keep investing in and organizing for Texas candidates who favor bringing casino gambling to the state.

That leaves Geren’s measure dependent on a Senate whose leadership is still contested. A simple majority could strip Goodwin’s powers once the chamber reconvenes in January.

Tech Report: 5 leadership lessons the music industry taught me

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spend enough time around live music and you quickly learn that the talent standing in the spotlight is only a small part of what makes a great show.
  • It has been revealed that spend enough time around live music and you rapidly learn that the talent standing in the spotlight is only a small part of what makes a great show.
  • Sources indicate that I’ve spent much of my career working in the music industry, from marketing and business development to managing independent venues and festivals, with stops along the way at Graceland, Fun Fun Fun Fest, DoStuff Media, and SXSW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spend enough time around live music and you quickly learn that the talent standing in the spotlight is only a small part of what makes a great show. Behind every successful performance is an entire team of talented people working together to make awesome moments happen. I’ve spent much of my career working in the music industry, from marketing and business development to managing independent venues and festivals, with stops along the way at Graceland, Fun Fun Fun Fest, DoStuff Media, and SXSW. I’ve also spent plenty of time playing music myself, including a period when I was pretty convinced I’d be the next Dave Matthews. Today, as Huntsville, Alabama’s Music Officer, I’ve found that many lessons I learned working with artists, agents, promoters, production teams, business executives, interns, and others have been just as valuable in government as in the music business. Here are five leadership lessons the music industry taught me that apply to most professions. 1. IF YOU SAY YOU’RE GOING TO DO SOMETHING, DO IT. Reliability is a highly underrated leadership quality. One of the quickest ways to lose your team’s confidence is surprisingly simple: Tell someone you’re going to do something and then don’t follow through. The lead guitarist might have incredible talent, but if they’re consistently late and unprepared, the band probably won’t be enthusiastic about working with them. Whether it’s finishing a project, making an introduction, or getting someone the information they need to move forward, people rely on those commitments. Not delivering on responsibilities can throw everything off course. Trust is ultimately built through what’s delivered. 2. YOU DON’T NEED TO BE THE SMARTEST PERSON IN THE ROOM. Nobody has all the answers, and being in a leadership position doesn’t automatically make your ideas the best ones. Some of the most creative and effective solutions I’ve encountered came from people closest to the work. Think about everything involved in producing a concert. The sound engineer understands things about audio the promoter probably doesn’t. The lighting director has perfected their craft. The artist, stage manager, marketing team, and venue operators have their own areas of expertise. How much harder would that operation be if everyone had to defer to one person who believed they knew more than everybody else? Create an environment where people feel valued and empowered to speak up, challenge ideas, and suggest better ways of doing things. 3. SOMETIMES THE BEST LEADERS GET OUT OF THE WAY. Musicians, technicians, stagehands, managers, security staff, and ticket sellers have specific responsibilities. When everyone knows what they’re doing, the operation runs so smoothly that most in the audience don’t think about the work happening behind the scenes. Sometimes a well-intentioned person jumping in to “help” can make things harder. The same applies to leadership. If you’ve assembled a great team, trust people to do their jobs. Your team should know you’re there when they need resources or guidance, but there’s a fine line between supporting and micromanaging. 4. BE A CHAMELEON WITHOUT BEING FAKE. In music, I worked with artists, business executives, concert promoters, venue operators, and community organizations. In government, I’ve added elected officials, city departments, and other stakeholders to that mix. Each group has its own priorities and communication styles. Learn how to adapt to those environments without compromising who you are. Understand the room you’re walking into. What matters to and motivates the people you’re talking with? What do they need to understand to make a decision? There’s a distinction between adapting your communication and claiming expertise you don’t have. Don’t change your values based on who’s in the room and don’t underestimate how quickly talented, experienced people can recognize when someone isn’t being genuine. 5. EARN THE RIGHT TO TAKE BIGGER SWINGS. Making the transition into local government from a music industry career came with culture shock. The music business naturally rewards creativity, experimentation, and taking risks. Government, for good reason, places greater emphasis on process, accountability, and responsibly allocating public resources. Those two approaches don’t have to be mutually exclusive. Some of the most meaningful progress happens when you bring an entrepreneurial mindset into an environment not accustomed to doing things differently. The key is understanding that you must earn the trust to experiment. Plenty of people seem more interested in being viewed as innovative rather than doing the work necessary to make their ideas successful. Making a bold move to prove you’re a bold leader isn’t a good strategy. Instead, focus on building credibility through consistent execution, responsible decisions, and a track record of delivering results. Trust is organizational capital. When you follow through on a commitment, solve a problem, or demonstrate sound judgment, you build more of it. Eventually, that credibility allows you to propose bigger ideas and challenge conventional thinking. These calculated risks might otherwise struggle to gain support. When you do take substantial swings, be thoughtful about potential consequences. Make sure the people involved understand the vision, the risks, and what you’re trying to accomplish. The goal should be to build something meaningful that creates opportunities and continues delivering value years down the road. LEADERS: IT’S NOT ALL ABOUT YOU The most important things I’ve learned about leadership came from working alongside talented people who knew how to get things done under pressure, and without much recognition. The best live performances are successful because people understand their roles, trust one another, communicate effectively, and take pride in contributing to something bigger than themselves. The same is true of great organizations. While the headliner gets applause, the entire team makes the show possible. Great leaders make sure everyone gets a standing ovation. Matt Mandrella is music officer of the City of Huntsville.

#23966. Industry News: 22 leadership insights on ensuring accountability without instilling fear
